macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as Dow gains about 1%
items.summary: U.S. stocks advanced Tuesday, led by the Dow, which rose about 1% to 52,485.50. The S&P 500 gained 0.4% and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.2% as investors rotated toward healthcare and value shares.[3]

items.title: Oil prices remain elevated amid geopolitical risks
items.summary: Brent crude climbed above $110 a barrel, a five-month high, as Middle East violence and uncertainty over possible U.S. sanctions relief for Russian energy exports raised supply concerns.[4][5]

items.title: European and Asian shares retreat
items.summary: European shares fell for a second consecutive session, with the STOXX 600 down 0.6%, while Asian markets broadly declined as higher oil prices pressured risk sentiment and investors awaited major technology earnings.[4][5]

items.title: Fed seen in no rush to raise rates
items.summary: Recent comments from Federal Reserve officials, including Chair Kevin Warsh, indicated that policymakers are not in a hurry to raise interest rates again, despite inflation risks from higher energy prices.[2][5]

items.title: People’s Bank of China leaves lending rates unchanged
items.summary: The PBOC kept the one-year Loan Prime Rate at 3.00% and the five-year rate at 3.50%, matching expectations and signaling no change in near-term monetary policy.[8]

items.title: Netflix and SpaceX earnings in focus
items.summary: Investors awaited quarterly results from Netflix and SpaceX after the close. Netflix was expected to report slower third-quarter revenue growth, while SpaceX was forecast to post $12.74 billion in quarterly revenue.[2][5]

items.title: GM shares fall after outlook signals pressure
items.summary: General Motors shares dropped more than 8% after the automaker warned of pressure from higher commodity costs and weaker truck sales.[3]

items.title: 3M raises outlook and expands Amazon data-center partnership
items.summary: 3M shares gained 5.9% after the company raised its full-year profit forecast and expanded its data-center partnership with Amazon, including a warrant valued at more than $521 million.[3]

items.title: OpenAI reportedly seeks $30 billion in funding
items.summary: Reports that OpenAI is seeking approximately $30 billion in new funding added to investor focus on the scale and financing of artificial-intelligence investment.[7]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $82,000 as crypto ETFs see mixed flows
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly reached $83,000 and traded around $82,000 as spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $526.6 million in net inflows. Spot Ethereum ETFs posted about $103.3 million in net outflows, while roughly $299.9 million in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours.

items.title: CFTC advances voluntary framework for crypto platforms
items.summary: The CFTC is advancing Reg CAM, a proposed framework intended to let crypto trading platforms voluntarily enter a unified nationwide regulatory regime after the Clarity Act stalled in Congress.

items.title: EU adds nine crypto service providers under MiCA
items.summary: ESMA added nine crypto-asset service providers to its MiCA registration list, bringing the reported total to 375 registered providers across the European Union.

items.title: JPMorgan expands JPM Coin to Ethereum
items.summary: JPMorgan Asset Management is expanding JPM Coin to Ethereum, allowing approved institutional clients to transfer dollar deposits and settle eligible digital-asset transactions on the network.

items.title: Ethereum Glamsterdam upgrade scheduled for Hoodi testnet
items.summary: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade is scheduled to activate on the Hoodi testnet on October 26. Planned changes include enshrined proposer-builder separation, block-level access lists and revised gas accounting, with the Hoodi gas limit set to rise to 200 million.

items.title: Qubic halts mainnet after wallet drain
items.summary: Qubic halted its mainnet following a reported wallet-drain incident affecting 1,404 accounts. The event was reported alongside broader blockchain developments including Pump.fun’s launch of perpetual futures trading through Hyperliquid.

items.title: Yuga Labs launches Mudwater physical and Solana NFT collection
items.summary: Yuga Labs launched Mudwater, a collection of physical Bored Ape Yacht Club cards paired with on-chain non-fungible tokens on Solana.

items.title: Crypto lending vault deposits surpass $10 billion
items.summary: Deposits in crypto lending vaults reportedly exceeded $10 billion, up from about $4 billion at the beginning of last year, highlighting increased demand for yield-oriented digital-asset strategies.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: MiniMax and DeepSeek release faster, cheaper AI models
items.summary: MiniMax launched M3.1 Flash, a mixture-of-experts model designed for AI agents that reportedly triples inference speed and cuts task costs by 70%. DeepSeek also introduced V4.1-Flash-1017, reducing coding-task costs through faster processing and shorter responses.

items.title: Reflection AI releases open-weight Beam model
items.summary: Reflection AI reportedly released Beam under the Apache 2.0 license. The 501-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model supports a one-million-token context window and is positioned for advanced coding and agent workloads.

items.title: Meta unveils open-weight Muse Spark model
items.summary: Meta reportedly introduced an open-weight Muse Spark model focused on coding, allowing developers to download and customize it. The release is part of a broader push toward highly capable, openly available models.

items.title: Meta announces Wonder and Wonder Full frontier models
items.summary: Meta reportedly unveiled two new frontier models, Wonder and Wonder Full, claiming performance comparable with leading OpenAI and Anthropic systems based on benchmark results cited by the company.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Alphabet reportedly released Gemini 4 Argon for developers and businesses worldwide, targeting complex coding and cybersecurity tasks after delays and leadership changes at DeepMind.

items.title: Microsoft completes pretraining for MAI-Base-2
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly finished pretraining its MAI-Base-2 model, described as having 2.8 trillion parameters, and is moving the system into post-training.

items.title: Microsoft launches Guardian Agents
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly introduced Guardian Agents, a feature designed to monitor and oversee AI agents deployed by organizations as part of its broader Project Perception initiative.

items.title: Nvidia releases enterprise models for AI agents
items.summary: Nvidia reportedly made Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt 74B-A9B available, positioning them for enterprise agent workloads. The company said Super VL completes some agentic tasks faster than competing models after post-training.

items.title: AWS releases TorchNeuron for Trainium migration
items.summary: AWS reportedly launched TorchNeuron, enabling AI startups to move PyTorch applications to the company’s Trainium accelerators and potentially reduce dependence on competing AI hardware ecosystems.

items.title: Cloudflare previews Clairic extraction model
items.summary: Cloudflare reportedly introduced Clairic, a new extraction-model category aimed at processing unstructured data more quickly, cheaply, and accurately than general-purpose large language models.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Steam Next Fest launches with 7,100 playable demos
items.summary: Steam Next Fest has begun with roughly 7,100 playable game demos, alongside updated discovery and filtering tools for browsing the event.

items.title: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 premieres on Netflix
items.summary: The second season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners is now available on Netflix, featuring a new story and a different group of protagonists from the first season.

items.title: Monster Hunter Wilds demo arrives on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Capcom has launched a free Prologue demo for Monster Hunter Wilds on Nintendo Switch 2, including local multiplayer and transferable save data.

items.title: League of Legends Worlds 2026 Play-In viewership falls
items.summary: The Worlds 2026 Play-In stage reportedly peaked at 1,021,367 concurrent viewers, a 59.2% decline from the previous year’s peak.

items.title: Xbox strategist sparks debate over AI use in games
items.summary: Xbox Business Strategist Brandon Stirrup argued that the games industry understates its use of artificial intelligence after demonstrating an AI-assisted game project. The comments prompted significant backlash, and his social-media account was reportedly deleted.

items.title: A Game About Digging A Hole Together announced for December
items.summary: Rokaplay and Mipumi Games announced that the cooperative follow-up to A Game About Digging a Hole will launch on December 4, 2026, across PC, consoles, and Nintendo Switch 2, with Xbox Game Pass availability.

items.title: Flutter plans up to 1,400 UK and Ireland redundancies
items.summary: Flutter Entertainment announced a restructuring of its UK and Ireland business that could result in up to 1,400 redundancies, affecting the broader betting and gaming sector.

items.title: GameSquare highlights expected Grand Theft Auto VI impact
items.summary: GameSquare published research describing a potential Grand Theft Auto VI effect, including possible changes in workplace attendance, entertainment spending, and sports viewership around the game’s launch.
